content: WikiDoc provides a reference management system that allows users to insert references directly into their text using PubMed ID numbers. Additionally, users can click on the reference to directly access the cited article. Typically, in traditional referencing methods, users would insert a number in the text (e.g., (1)) and then manually add the corresponding reference at the end of the article. However, WikiDoc discourages this approach. Instead, it offers an automated reference manager with several advantages: References are automatically numbered. References move with the text when it is relocated. Clicking on a reference takes the user directly to the cited article. To use the WikiDoc reference manager, users insert a code for the reference immediately after the relevant text. This code is generated using a software program. The process for using the reference manager is as follows: 1. Locate the desired article on PubMed by searching for it. 2. Copy the PubMed ID (PMID) number, which is typically found at the bottom of the article's abstract. For example, a PMID might look like this: `PMID: 19032997`. 3. Paste the PMID into a software program designed to generate Wiki language code for references. Examples of such software include: SUMSearch Biomedical Citation Maker DOI Wikipedia reference generator DTU Informatics PMID to Cite journal OttoBib Dave's Template Filler 4. 5. Submit the PMID to generate the Wiki language code. 6. Copy the generated Wiki language code. For example, the output for the PMID `19032997` might look like this: ``` {{cite journal |author=Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al '' |title=Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 |journal=Am Heart J |volume=156 |issue=6 |pages=1035–44 |year=2008 |month=December |pmid=19032997 |doi=10 1016/j ahj 2008 07 029 |url=}} ``` 7. Paste this code directly into the text where the superscript reference number should appear. For example, if you were referencing the above article, you might write: Gibson et al recently summarized the improvements made in clinical outcomes as a result of 15 years of quality improvement efforts in the NRMI registry {{cite journal |author=Gibson CM, Pride YB, Frederick PD, ''et al '' |title=Trends in reperfusion strategies, door-to-needle and door-to-balloon times, and in-hospital mortality among patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction enrolled in the National Registry of Myocardial Infarction from 1990 to 2006 |journal=Am Heart J |volume=156 |issue=6 |pages=1035–44 |year=2008 |month=December |pmid=19032997 |doi=10 1016/j ahj 2008 07 029 |url=}}. This would generate a reference that appears as a clickable superscript number in the text, linking to the full citation at the bottom of the article. If you prefer not to use the reference manager, you can manually insert references. To do this: 1. Place `<ref>` immediately after the sentence where you want the footnote number to appear. 2. Type the reference text between the `<ref>` tags. For example: ``` <ref>Author Name. Title of the Article. Journal Name. Year;Volume(Issue):Page Numbers.</ref> ``` 3. If you plan to use the same reference multiple times, assign a name to the reference using the format `<ref name=ReferenceName>`. To display references at the bottom of the article, use the following code: ``` <references /> ``` This will generate a list of references in small font, formatted in two columns, with clickable links to the original articles and abstracts.
